author: John Baker
title: Poll Shows Major Shift Among Young Male Voters - NewsBreak
text: The Democratic Party has drawn some backlash for launching a $20 million initiative called SAM (Speaking with American Men), aimed at regaining the support of male voters. Harvard polls have shown that over half of men under 30 favored President Donald Trump, prompting a strategic shift from Democratic leaders. The Democratic National Committee’s website lists support for multiple groups while excluding men, which has raised questions regarding the party plans to win back male voters. For years, portrayals of “toxic masculinity” have left many men feeling marginalized. There’s growing recognition that many men are struggling to get by, lacing positions of power. Harris 2024 Campaign Rapid Response Director Ammar Moussa said, “I think both Ilyse and John are smart, talented operatives who have very good intentions.” Moussa added, “I think broadly, writ large — and this is hardly unique to Ilyse and John — it is beyond embarrassing that in the year 2025, the Democratic Party wants to spend tens of millions of dollars to figure out how to talk to half of the population. It really isn’t that hard.” The gap between Democratic messaging and the realities of many working-class men reveals a major disconnect. Disparaging remarks from party figures have reinforced negative stereotypes, deepening alienation. Strategists have noted that rebuilding support will require a shift in both tone and approach to show greater respect and understanding. Moussa said, “This really isn’t rocket science. We’re treating young men and working-class voters like they’re foreign aliens who just visited Earth who are speaking a different language. And to some degree, we are [speaking a different language], for a multitude of reasons — mostly because the Democratic Party is staffed with operatives who no longer reflect what the electorate looks like anymore. And that’s a problem.” John Baker covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
